newsitem.title: USA: Union Carbide reports sharply lower income.
newsitem.headline: Union Carbide reports sharply lower income.

text.p: Union Carbide Corp. Monday posted a big drop in third-quarter net earnings due to the poor performance of its basic chemicals business.

The Danbury, Conn.-based company said it earned $161 million, or $1.19 a share, on sales of $1.53 billion. That compared with earnings of $277 million, or $1.96 a share, on sales of $1.50 billion in the third quarter of last year.

It said that weak prices for ethylene glycol and a jump in feedstock costs sharply lowered the operating profit of its basic chemicals and polymers business to $40 million from $121 million a year ago.

Union Carbide said the specialities and intermediates business, which makes products for the paint and coatings industry as well as chemicals for pharmaceuticals, automotive, industrial lubricant manufacturers, had a strong operating profit of $202 million, up from $115 million in the third quarter of last year.
Union Carbide's stock was off 62.5 cents at $43.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
